newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-up $1.00 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-up $1.00 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct hog prices early Wednesday were steady to $1.00 per cwt higher amid brisk competition from packers for reduced hog supplies, livestock dealers said.
Hog movement was slowed by improved weather in the Corn Belt, which allowed producers to return to fieldwork in some areas following wet, cold weather late last week, they said.

Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota hogs sold $0.50 to $1.00 higher at $52.00 to $53.00 in the country and $54.00 to $55.00 at plants. Illinois hogs sold $1.00 higher at $52.50 to $53.50 in the country and $54.00 to $54.50 plants, sources there said.
Indiana hogs sold $0.50 higher, but could go $1.00 higher as the day progresses, sources there said. Indiana hogs in the country sold at $51.50 to $52.00 and up to $53.50 at plants.
"This feels like one of those days that's going to get better as it goes on," one central Indiana buyer said.
Ohio hogs sold steady at $50.00 to $51.00 in the country and $52.00 to $53.00 at plants, but prices could also firm later, a dealer in southern Ohio said.
Cash hog prices also were supported by ideas that hog supplies would remain tight going into next week, unless rain disrupts fieldwork again and allow farmers time to sell hogs.
